{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce service",
      "body": "The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: ... }`, whereas the previous schema `.parse()` returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result directly as `credential.key` replaces the credential with a validation-result wrapper. This also affects installations with syncing disabled: after the first successful refresh, subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse the stored credentials. Persist the result's `data` instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Replace computed schema keys with actual token-field validation",
      "body": "`z.string().toString()` does not define a wildcard property: it produces the literal key `[object Object]`. Both computed keys resolve to that same key, so the optional unknown schema overwrites the numeric schema. Since Zod objects strip unknown properties by default, a sync response such as `{ access_token: \"token\", expires_in: 3600 }` loses its expiry and any refresh token. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office 365 cannot persist the refreshed expiry. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers",
      "body": "The sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, but several callers retain the return contract of their original refresh function. Google Calendar and both Zoho services read `.data`, while HubSpot reads `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn` directly. None of these properties exists on a Fetch Response, regardless of its JSON body. Enabling syncing therefore makes those refresh paths throw or use undefined tokens. Establish a consistent response contract and deserialize/adapt the response in each caller."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace existing refresh tokens with a placeholder",
      "body": "The literal `\"refresh_token\"` is inserted whenever a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 explicitly accepts refresh responses without a new refresh token and merges the parsed data into the existing credentials. This new placeholder overwrites the valid saved refresh token, so the next refresh fails. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement; do not fabricate one in the shared parser."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint",
      "body": "The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID and is sent externally as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential row's ID. These IDs are unrelated. The parent application will either find no matching user or return another user's Bigin token, potentially causing CRM writes against the wrong account. Carry `credential.userId` through to this method instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Delegate Salesforce refreshes when credential sharing is enabled",
      "body": "The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce instead of using the configured credential-sync endpoint. For externally managed credentials, Cal.com may only have an access token and no usable refresh token; this request then fails before the connection is constructed, even if the supplied access token is still valid. Route this refresh through the same delegation mechanism as the other integrations and use the returned token in the connection."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name",
      "body": "The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: \"zoom\"`, and the new webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same slug to store and retrieve credentials cannot resolve this refresh request. Pass `\"zoom\"` here to keep the inbound and outbound contracts consistent."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Authenticate requests that retrieve external access tokens",
      "body": "The outbound request contains only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no secret, signature, or authorization header. An ordinary HTTP sync endpoint therefore has no application-level way to distinguish Cal.com from a caller requesting another user's token. A protected endpoint must reject these requests; accepting them without additional infrastructure exposes tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound protocol rather than requiring an unauthenticated token lookup."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make initial webhook credential creation atomic",
      "body": "The lookup and create are separate operations without serialization. Two concurrent deliveries for the same new user/app pair can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Later deliveries update only whichever row `findFirst` selects, leaving the other credential stale and potentially causing duplicate integration processing. Make this operation idempotent under concurrent webhook delivery."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Clear invalid status when replacing credentials through the webhook",
      "body": "The update path replaces only `key`. Integrations such as Google Calendar and Zoom mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authentication failures. Sending replacement credentials through this webhook returns success but leaves that invalid status intact, so an external reconnection does not restore a healthy installed credential. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Adapt Webex validation to the delegated token response",
      "body": "The new helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A response following the delegated-refresh contract is always rejected as invalid, preventing Webex meeting operations after token expiry. Add a delegated-response adapter and preserve the necessary existing credential metadata."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce service
findings.body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations.

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: ... }`, whereas the previous schema `.parse()` returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result directly as `credential.key` replaces the credential with a validation-result wrapper. This also affects installations with syncing disabled: after the first successful refresh, subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse the stored credentials. Persist the result's `data` instead.

findings.title: Replace computed schema keys with actual token-field validation
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` does not define a wildcard property: it produces the literal key `[object Object]`. Both computed keys resolve to that same key, so the optional unknown schema overwrites the numeric schema. Since Zod objects strip unknown properties by default, a sync response such as `{ access_token: "token", expires_in: 3600 }` loses its expiry and any refresh token. Zoom then computes a NaN expiry, and Office 365 cannot persist the refreshed expiry. Define and preserve the actual supported response fields.

findings.title: Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, but several callers retain the return contract of their original refresh function. Google Calendar and both Zoho services read `.data`, while HubSpot reads `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn` directly. None of these properties exists on a Fetch Response, regardless of its JSON body. Enabling syncing therefore makes those refresh paths throw or use undefined tokens. Establish a consistent response contract and deserialize/adapt the response in each caller.

findings.title: Do not replace existing refresh tokens with a placeholder
findings.body: The literal `"refresh_token"` is inserted whenever a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 explicitly accepts refresh responses without a new refresh token and merges the parsed data into the existing credentials. This new placeholder overwrites the valid saved refresh token, so the next refresh fails. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement; do not fabricate one in the shared parser.

findings.title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint
findings.body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID and is sent externally as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential row's ID. These IDs are unrelated. The parent application will either find no matching user or return another user's Bigin token, potentially causing CRM writes against the wrong account. Carry `credential.userId` through to this method instead.

findings.title: Delegate Salesforce refreshes when credential sharing is enabled
findings.body: The new Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce instead of using the configured credential-sync endpoint. For externally managed credentials, Cal.com may only have an access token and no usable refresh token; this request then fails before the connection is constructed, even if the supplied access token is still valid. Route this refresh through the same delegation mechanism as the other integrations and use the returned token in the connection.

findings.title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name
findings.body: The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: "zoom"`, and the new webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same slug to store and retrieve credentials cannot resolve this refresh request. Pass `"zoom"` here to keep the inbound and outbound contracts consistent.

findings.title: Authenticate requests that retrieve external access tokens
findings.body: The outbound request contains only a numeric user ID and app slug, with no secret, signature, or authorization header. An ordinary HTTP sync endpoint therefore has no application-level way to distinguish Cal.com from a caller requesting another user's token. A protected endpoint must reject these requests; accepting them without additional infrastructure exposes tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound protocol rather than requiring an unauthenticated token lookup.

findings.title: Make initial webhook credential creation atomic
findings.body: The lookup and create are separate operations without serialization. Two concurrent deliveries for the same new user/app pair can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Later deliveries update only whichever row `findFirst` selects, leaving the other credential stale and potentially causing duplicate integration processing. Make this operation idempotent under concurrent webhook delivery.

findings.title: Clear invalid status when replacing credentials through the webhook
findings.body: The update path replaces only `key`. Integrations such as Google Calendar and Zoom mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authentication failures. Sending replacement credentials through this webhook returns success but leaves that invalid status intact, so an external reconnection does not restore a healthy installed credential. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

findings.title: Adapt Webex validation to the delegated token response
findings.body: The new helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A response following the delegated-refresh contract is always rejected as invalid, preventing Webex meeting operations after token expiry. Add a delegated-response adapter and preserve the necessary existing credential metadata.
